EventName: Arkansas Enduro Series Finale | Round 4 | Mt. Nebo Enduro
EventNotes:
MT. NEBO ENDURO | NOVEMBER 21-22, 2026

We’re excited to return to the stunning Mount Nebo State Park! The Mt. Nebo Enduro is a mix of technical and flowy singletrack with stages for all levels. Perched high above the Arkansas River Valley, Mount Nebo offers amazing views.

Registration opens Friday, June 12th at 8am with participation based on a first-come, first-served basis. To create a rewarding enduro race experience, organizers reserve the right to limit overall event participation. Each participant’s entry includes:

  • One-day competition with up to 4-7 stages and 10-20 total miles of rider-designed racing with dedicated pre-race practice times the day prior to the race.
  • Sufficiently marked courses with maps emailed to participants the week of the event.
  • Lively mid-race aid stations with access to professional neutral mechanics and medical support.
  • Professional event timing with accuracy to the 1000th of a second and instant results.
  • Complimentary post-race meal and cold beverages (21+ for adult beverages, ID required) in a family-friendly festival setting.
  • Awards ceremony by category with prizes awarded 5 deep.

RACE VENUE

Mount Nebo is a prominent, flat-topped mountain mesa located in west-central Arkansas near Dardanelle. Rising 1,762 feet above sea level and soaring 1,350 feet directly out of the surrounding Arkansas River Valley, it is entirely enclosed by Mount Nebo State Park. Established in 1927, it serves as Arkansas's second-oldest state park and is a premier hub for outdoor recreation. 

Venue Address: 16728 West State Hwy. 155, Dardanelle, AR 72834

 

EVENT SCHEDULE

Final event schedule with packet pickup, official pre-ride, and start times will be released the week of the event. Arkansas Enduro Series events are rain or shine except under extreme circumstances. When permittable, an official pre-ride/practice will be scheduled the day prior to Race Day(s). The Race Director reserves the right to adjust the schedule due to any unforeseen circumstances.

FRIDAY |

  • Early pre-riding is allowed although some stages may in the proccess of being finishing marking.
  • 4PM-7PM | Early Check-In | Location TBA

SATURDAY |

  • 9AM-4PM | Check-In & Official Practice Day

SUNDAY | 

  • 8AM-10AM | Timing Chip Pick-Up according to Wave Times. Late Check-In available.
  • 9AM-3PM | Race Day
  • 4PM | Podium Awards

Arkansas Enduro Series events are rain or shine except under extreme circumstances. When possible, an official practice will be scheduled the day prior to Race Day(s). The Race Director reserves the right to adjust the schedule due to any unforeseen circumstances. 

 

DRY CAMPING - To book your campsite, visit the Arkansas State Parks reservation page. 

SAFETY - This is not the time to skimp on protective equipment. Helmets are required to be worn on course during official event times and we highly suggest a full-face helmet, knee pads, and elbow pads.

TEMPERATURE - In November, Mount Nebo, Arkansas experiences cool, crisp weather. Temperatures typically reach an average high in the mid-50s (50°F to 54°F) and drop to average nightly lows in the low-to-mid 30s (30°F to 35°F).

WATER & SNACKS - While hydration will be available at select locations on course, riders are encouraged to plan to carry at least 50-60 ounces of water and enough snacks to sustain themselves under strenuous exercise.

NICE TO HAVES - Bug spray, sunscreen, spare tubes, pump or CO2, plugs, patches and other parts.

DOGS - Dogs are allowed but are required to be on a leash at all times. No exceptions.

TRASH - If you pack it in, pack it out. We are guests. Please follow all event sustainability and recycling requests.

RACE DAY MEAL - A post-race meal will be provided to racers and volunteers on Race Days only. Redeemable meal tickets will be provided at the Registration & Timing tent. When possible, additional food trucks and other resources will be made available on-site for fans, family and friends.

WAIVER - All participants will be required to sign a waiver of liability prior to competing in the Arkansas Enduro Series.

REFUND POLICY - Arkansas Enduro Series events are rain or shine, and refunds will not be issued except under extreme circumstances. The Event Organizer reserves the right to adjust the schedule due to any unforeseen circumstances including rescheduling the event to a future date.

If participants choose to add additional Registration Protector through BikeReg, those claims are handled entirely by Allianz Global Assistance. For policy questions or to file a claim visit www.eventregistrationprotection.com or call 1-888-799-2832.

SERIES RULES - additional series information and rules available at www.arkansasenduroseries.com/rules.

Every year an event comes along that tests mental and physical strengths of its racers like no other. Pisgah Productions proudly presents the hardest (and most fun) thing you will do this year….. the DOUBLE DARE.

Teams of two riders will race to reach up to 10 checkpoints (CPs) per day, two days in a row. The race begins at 10AM on Saturday and every team must be back before 10PM. The race resumes at 6AM Sunday with 10 brand new checkpoints. Every team must finish before 6PM on Sunday. Teams ‘in the running’ should expect up to 70 miles of riding with 12,000-15,000 feet of climbing each day.

SINGLE-DARE! The one-day category at Double-Dare!!! Teams of two riders will race up to 10 checkpoints, in any order, and return to the start/finish the fastest. Checkpoint locations will remain secret until start time and there is no suggested route. Start time for the one-day category will be 10AM Saturday and Final cutoff will be 10PM.

For both DOUBLE-DARE and SINGLE-DARE:

There will be nothing at the checkpoints other than pre-existing landmarks. Every team must carry a reliable digital camera to photograph the landmarks as proof of being there.

Welcome to the Cross of the North registration page.  Come celebrate with us at New Belgium in Fort Collins for two days of exciting racing. For all of the event info, LIKE us on Facebook and FOLLOW us on Instagram and Twitter.

Also, please consider volunteering. It takes more than a village to make Cross of the North a success. Check out our volunteer signup.

Two things that you can refrain from to help ensure COTN's future at New Belgium:

  • Do not bring alcohol. New Belgium is a brewery, their beer is good, and you should buy it. Not to mention the fact that outside alcohol is prohibited by the terms of our event liquor license. In addition, all proceeds from alcohol sales are donated to support youth cycling through Send Town Bike Club!!
  • Do not park in the Buckingham neighborhood. Do not park or warm up on 1st, 2nd, or 3rd streets, on the south side of Buckingham, or any of the cross streets in the Buckingham neighborhood. New Belgium brings a lot of traffic to the neighborhood, and we want to respect their desire for peace and quiet.

Other things you should know:

1) 18 and Under race free, in Jr Categories and for $20 in any other categories.  Enter coupon code COTNJR2026 when you register.

2) Participants are required to have USA Cycling license. For SM 5, SW 5 and junior categories only, USA Cycling 1-day Beginner Licenses ($15) are available for purchase. 1-day licenses are available only to racers who have never held a USAC license with a higher category, Men/Junior Men and Women/Junior Women. USAC 1-Day Experienced license: $35, only available to former USAC members- category 1,2,3,4 men/women, and must be purchased online.

3) Team Tent locations (10'x10', 10'x20', 20'x20') are available at no charge. However, you must make a reservation. NO RESERVATION = NO TENT. Tents may be set up on Friday and left overnight Friday and Saturday, as long as they are properly weighted. We will provide drop-off instructions to registrants prior to race day. No team/club trailers will be allowed in club row.

4) Women entering Men’s Races: Women may enter any men’s race for which they are eligible by age, category, and any performance requirements. They may also enter categorized races for men that are up to one category lower than their women's category. For cyclo-cross events, category 1 women may enter men’s races up to two categories lower.

Master women may compete in men’s masters races as follows:

    (i) category 1 and 2 master women may enter men’s events for riders up to 10 years above their racing ages;
    (ii) category 3 and 4 master women may enter men’s events for riders up to 20 years above their racing ages.

When registering for Men’s races, especially those in a lower category, you may receive a warning message. Please acknowledge the message and complete the registration.


5) Registration closes Thursday Nov 19, 2025 at 5 p.m. MST. Race Day registration will be $50 per race. Juniors in Jr categories race free even with Race Day registration.

Race day registration and packet pickup close 45 minutes before each race group. NO EXCEPTIONS.

Adding a second race on the same day is only $20.

6) Friday Pre-ride: We will open the course 3pm-4pm on Friday for pre-ride. Pre-riders must sign a pre-ride waiver and follow race staff instructions. Riding without first signing a waiver, or failing to follow race staff instructions, may result in disqualification from the Saturday and/or Sunday races.

7) Callups: Callups will be based on CrossResults.com rankings. Athletes with no CrossResults.com ranking who pre-register will be called up ahead of athletes with no CrossResults.com ranking who do not pre-register. 

At the discretion of the chief referee, some waves may be split into separate categories and begin on separate whistles. The decision may be made based on overall safety of athletes (based on quantity of racers in wave), or based on providing more appropriate and equitable competitive playing field for the categories on the course at the same time.

Can you believe it’s our eighteenth year! Join us for Turkey Bike on  Saturday November 21st. If you haven't done Turkey Bike before here's how it works. Riders meet at Cycle Craft in Parsippany and roll out at 9:00 and head to King’s supermarket in Boonton to buy a bunch of turkeys. Then, we ride over to Smartworld Coffee in Denville where the Community Food Bank of New Jersey is there to receive the birds. The ride is fairly easy and you only have to carry your turkey for a few miles. We recommend using a sturdy back pack or pannier bags on a rack to carry your bird. String bags are not any fun to use and front baskets can be tricky to manage with a 20lb turkey in it. There is no entry fee so your only cost is the cost of the turkey that you pick out.

When you arrive at Smartworld we'll treat to you hot beverages and delicious snacks as our way of saying "thanks!" for participating. Riders then head back to Cycle Craft. It's a fun way to do something good!

Riders meet at Cycle Craft Parsippany with check in beginning at 8:00AM and the ride rolls at 9:00AM. If you have any questions please email brendan@cyclecraft.com

If you can't make the ride please consider making a $35 donation and we will buy and carry your turkey for you!

Here is a link to the Turkey Bike Route  https://ridewithgps.com/routes/44981418 It says 2024 but the route is the same this year

Cranksgiving Boise is an annual alleycat-style scavenger hunt on bikes. Teams of costumed cyclists ride around town on an odyssey to find the answers to trivia questions about local art and history, while also gathering all the items necessary to fill Thanksgiving food boxes that will be donated to Saint Vincent de Paul for its program that helps feed families in need throughout the Treasure Valley. This is the 11th Annual edition of this fun biking event. 

Cranskgiving Boise will take place on Saturday, November 21st, starting and ending at  Idaho River Sports, 601 N Whitewater Park Blvd., Boise.  Packet pick-up starts at 10:00 a.m., with the event starting promptly at 11:00 a.m.

The ideal Cranksgiving team is four people. While teams can have up to six riders, if you have more riders than that, we strongly encourage you to create another team. The goal is to feed as many families as possible and having more teams helps achieve that goal. 

We are charging a modest $10 to register a team to cover our costs of hosting registration on this website and other expenses involved with staging this event.

Costumes are encouraged! There will be prizes for the first three teams by time, for the team bringing in the biggest turkey, and the teams with the best costumes, as decided by a vote of participants.

Cranksgiving is made possible this year by the generous support of Ketlinski Law Office.

For the latest information on Cranksgiving Boise, visit our Facebook page.

EventName: Martha’s Vineyard Adventure Tour with Mike and Mary
EventNotes:
COME Ride Martha’s Vineyard with MTB legends, Mike and Mary - along with our friends of New England Expedition Riders (NEER)!  It will be a fun day of exploring the island’s back routes and trails on mountain or gravel bikes … We will ride a steady pace, intermediate to advanced - over mixed terrain with options to do shorter or longer routes depending on the crew…@25-30 miles…3-4 hours of GOOD Mixed terrain BIKE FUN :-)  

Details : We will meet around 10:30am in Vineyard Haven near the ferry, (off island riders can catch a 9:30am ferry (from Woods Hole).  We should be back from our ride around 3-3:30pm - so a 3:45pm or 5pm ferry back would be the earliest return).

It is an incredibly quiet and beautiful time of year to ride bikes!  

The route plan : A new configuration of quiet back routes through forest woodlands and to some gorgeous vantage points... We will take mid ride refreshment breaks and return back to our starting spot, for libations and a bowl of something hot around 3pm.   It is a no drop ride.

There will be ride leaders in the case we need to split into smaller groups.  GPS route will be available.

This ride will be operated with our friend Patria of New England Expedition Riders (NEER).  For Insurance purposes, we are requiring NEER membership in the  registration cost.

To register and purchase your annual NEER membership visit:

https://www.newenglandexpeditionriders.com/rides-events/mv-adventure-2025

or click the BIKE reg links

NEER is a fantastic group of hearty riders who love to get our all year round! Check them out!

Bikes:  we recommend MTBs (hardtail or dual suspension if you prefer to not feel the bumps ;-)). A Gravel bike with minimum 38-40mm tires is possible too!  We would like to get out on more trails than in past editions… It will not be an overly technical ride - but our island trails can be bumpy and leaves are down so larger volume tires are preferred for comfort….

There will be 2 mechanics on the ride (MIKE and Patria ;-) and We will have our tool kits on us (and a floor pump in our van…for before the ride) if needed...  

Please bring your bike in perfect working order…. and what you need to have a successful ride.

Go Nuts Regionals (GNR) eMTB Rules as follows: 
1) Maximum 750watts - assistance up to 20 miles per hour - Pedaling assistance only. No hand or foot throttle allowed. Automatic disqualification. Bicycles must remain locked, i.e., no modification of wheel sensor from factory circumference or any other modification to manipulate the factory set speed of the bike.
2) Throttle mechanisms are prohibited.
3) Studded tires are prohibited.
4) It is forbidden to change e-bike during the event even if the rider finishes the event with the same race plate.
5) It is forbidden to recharge the e-bike or battery in the technical zone during the GNR event.
6) Technical assistance consists of the replacement or repairs of any part of the e-bike at the exception of the frame, wheels or battery.
7) Riders age categories are 18 and under, 19-39, 40-49 and 50 plus for Classes; Amateurs, Experts and Open Pro. 
8) Riders can only use the battery in place on their bike and cannot carry or switch out an additional battery during the competition.
9) Race course length will be 4.5 - 7 miles depending on difficulty. Steeper climbs and more technical than normal XC will be tested on some courses. Each category will start an hour apart and should be completed within their hour.
10) Races will be conducted regardless of weather conditions.  In the event of rain or other unfavorable conditions, it may be necessary to alter the order of the event schedule, including but not limited to, adjusting the length of the race or delaying or stopping the program completely.  Should a delay occur, every effort will be made to resume the schedule in a timely fashion if conditions significantly improve.
11) No headphones, earphones or sound devices permitted. Horns and bells are permitted.
12) Riders are required to wear the appropriate helmet. Other protective gear is optional; gloves, goggles, elbow/knee guards, etc.
13) Shirt, shoes, and pants/shorts required. Clipless or flat pedals are both permitted.
15) An E-Mountain Bike is a bike operated with two energy sources, human pedal power and an electric engine, which only provides assistance when the rider is pedaling.
16) The course will the taped and marked. Any rider cutting the course will be disqualified.
17) Any behavior deemed in appropriate or unsportsmanlike like conduct will not be tolerated. Verbal or physical infractions will result in a disqualification.

Severe weather policy
Unless otherwise posted, race will be held. Safety of all racers is our main priority. If there is a delay or cancellation due to weather conditions, racers are responsible for checking information posted by director.
The information will be posted on the homepage of website, social network avenues, and via email up to 72 hours prior to the race.

Transfer/Refund Policy
There will be no registration refunds once registration is processed. We will allow transfers to upcoming races. All transfers must be requested 10 days prior and is only allowed for races that were rescheduled. Transfers will not be allowed 10 days before race or after race.

GILLIES CREEK CX IS HERE!

SAUNDAY, NOVEMBER 22, 2026

It's cowbells echoing across the course. Friends screaming your name while you're questioning several recent life choices. Kids racing. First-timers discovering CX. Veterans fighting for one more place. Mud if we're lucky. Dust if we're not.

Race it. Heckle it. Volunteer at it. Bring the family. Bring your friends.

Just don't hear about how much fun everyone had afterward and wish you'd been there.

Get registered. Get stoked. We'll see you on the line … or behind the tape. ??

 

USA CYCLING LICENSES

  • GILLIES CREEK CX is a USA Cycling-sanctioned event.
  • Racers must have a valid USA Cycling license or purchase an eligible one-day license.
  • One-day licenses will be available for racers who need one.
  • Final 2026 permit number and one-day license pricing will be posted once confirmed.

85 RACERS. LET’S DO THIS.

Putting on a CX race takes permits, insurance, officials and a whole bunch of behind-the-scenes stuff.

  • We need 85 PAID registrations by Monday, November 16 to make THUNDERCROSS happen. If we don’t hit 85, we’ll have to cancel and everyone registered will receive a full refund.

  • Planning to race? Register early. It helps make sure we all get to race.

  • 85 is the magic number. Let’s get there.

RACING MORE THAN ONCE?

  • We like your style.
  • Add additional race categories for just $10 each per day when you register.
  • Simply select every event you want to race during registration and BikeReg will automatically apply the discount.
  • More racing. More heckling. More opportunities to tell everyone that this was definitely your “B race.”


BRINGING A PIT BIKE?

Fancy.

An additional bib plate for your pit bike is $5. Just select the pit-bike option when you register.

Because nothing says cyclocross like bringing another bicycle specifically for when the first bicycle becomes too muddy.


RACER CHECK-IN

Check-in for each race closes 30 minutes before that race starts, so give yourself time to get checked in, pin your number, inspect the course, warm up, and contemplate your tire-pressure decisions.

NO WALK-UPS. YES. REALLY  

Registration stays open until 6:00 PM the day before the race, so you've got plenty of time to make the excellent decision to race.

All race additions and category changes must also be completed through BikeReg before registration closes.

“But what if I'm not 100% sure I can make it?”

We hear you, cupcake.

That's why we've got a no-risk registration policy.

So register. Put it on the calendar. Start practicing your remounts.

Seriously. You can do this.


 VACX CHAMPS - YOU EARNED IT

Were you a 2025 VACX Champion? Your championship perks are still good here.

USE CODE 26VACXCHAMP to get your $10 entry. 

Then make sure you use your code BEFORE registration closes. Don't leave those hard-earned champ perks sitting on the sidelines.


LET'S GO!

Whether you’re gunning for the podium or just out to support, we can’t wait to see you for an epic day of cyclocross action.

EventNotes:
Boy howdy, it's Fall Fuckaround time again! Once again we're riding to benefit The Lancaster Conservancy and The Marietta Woods Project. We spend a lot of time enjoying these lands and we wanna chip in. 

 

Morning of:

We'll be starting at the shop, 414 N. Mary Street, Lancaster. There is plenty of free street parking in every direction around the shop. If it's raining and you need a dry staging area, there is a reasonably priced parking garage just a few blocks away at 220 N. Water Street, Lancaster. Our friends at Endo Cafe will have the coffee trailer there to keep you warm and caffeinated before we shove off.  West Art will be open at 7am with coffee and pastries just a few blocks up Lemon Street.  If you're looking for a full breakfast, Prince Street Cafe will be open at 7am and Lancaster's Central Market will be open at 6am. If you've never been, Central Market is the social hub of Lancaster and is worth getting up a little early to see. Whatever you do, be at the shop by 9:30 and be ready to roll at 10:00. 

 

The ride:

There are two courses, however both courses also have an alternate route for folks with road bikes (and road bike shoes.) All courses are linked below. There are no course markings, please download the course to a computer or use Ride With GPS. You will have phone reception the entire day, so if things get fucky, just find your way home using your phone. 

The long course has a substantial (3/4 mile?) hike-a-bike section, non-road shoes are highly recommended. Both courses follow the length of Suzy's Hole, which is light singletrack with a couple very easy creek crossings. The only aid station on the day is immediately after the Suzy's/Trolley Road trail section. Mom and Dad von Fancypants will be serving up the treats. 

After the aid station there's a short section of chunky railroad ballast, then a bunch of miles of some of the most beautiful rail trail anywhere. While on the rail trail, riders will cross the Safe Harbor bridge, which provides expansive views of the Susquehanna River. After leaving the rail trail, you'll wind through Millersville and back to the  shop. 

 

Long Course: https://ridewithgps.com/routes/38049384

Long Course (Road): https://ridewithgps.com/routes/41451896

Short Course: https://ridewithgps.com/routes/41098048

Short Course (Road): https://ridewithgps.com/routes/41451829

 

The Dirtbag After-Party:

We'll have fire pits to stand around. Cabalar will be open with the meats and the non-meats (OMG SRSLY the falafel burger is a revelation). Lancaster celebrity Drew Bell will be there to regale us with stories over the fire pits and serve us Endo Tunies (sorry hornballs, he's married). Lancaster's vegan comfort food spot, Bad Garden Kitchen, will be open just a few blocks away. The Pennsylvania Dirtbags will be there too- we have no idea what they have planned, and for liability's sake, we don't want to know. 

 

The Big Dumb Awards Show and Raffle:

Back for 2025: The Bill & Ted Awards for Excellence in the field of Being Excellent. The trophies are recycled. The awards have no value. But GOSH DARNIT the sentiment is real. Last year, for the third consecutive year, the Yinzer contingent went home with the most hardware (but no police citation). Past awards have included: The Sarah Woshe Award for General Gangstery, The Leo Quisimbing Spirit of Gravel Award, The Scotty Clark “Clean Drawers” Award, Least Improved, Best Dressed, Worst Bike, Worst Dressed, Best Bike, The Linette Award for Best Colors, and Least Offensive Odor. Also back for 2026 is the Highest Finisher award, although the homies from Action Wheels are always hard to beat here. (One year they finished so high that they left the trophy on the roof of their team car and drove off with it up there, never to be seen again.) Other awards categories will be decided on the fly. All of them will be stupid.  

This year's raffle will be bigger and a little less of a clusterfuck. Raffles will be announced every half hour starting at 3:00. Winners must be present, but raffles will be going off every 30 minutes for the duration of the evening. The big stuff will be raffled after the awards ceremony.

 

Please don't take any of it too seriously.

EventName: The Ride Series MTB Skills Clinics: DROP PROGRESSION & JUMP PROGRESSION NOV 27TH
EventNotes:
The Ride Series is different. Your expectations should be high as you enter the hospitality of our classroom setting. A comfortable Kijaro chair awaits your presence and the cover our 10x20 tents provides reprieve from the elements. Prepare yourself to be immersed in an environment that provides the perfect opportunity for you to be open to embracing and practicing the proper technique. Instant feedback from our coaching staff will have you progressing like never before! Are YOU ready??

DROP PROGRESSION: Ground School and SP Skills Park 

Welcome to a world where Physics, Gravity, and the engineering of your bike are embraced to help guide you off drops like never before. It's not rocket science, it's rational thought manifesting in you being more confident and landing drops with more stability than you ever thought possible. 

JUMP PROGRESSION Session: Ground School and All American Heroes Jumpline

This event is all about getting comfortable in the air. That starts with a solid understanding of what it takes to get into the air properly. It's also critical to get as MANY reps as possible in a controlled environment and that's what the TRS ground school setting gives you.

Our Pro level coaches break down the dynamics involved with jumping a bike. Based on over 70 years experience, they guide you through their real world experience and give you key insight and cues on what to do and also what not to do. 

After showcasing the proper technique, you'll work through a series of reps and the distance will incrementally increase as your comfort level increases. Analysis and feedback using slow motion video will have you "busting big" in no time.

There's no substitute for experience when it comes to jumping a bike. The only problem is that experience in the right setting can be hard to come by. You'll get tons reps on our jump lines and receive valuable feedback in the moment.
RIDERS MUST HAVE:
- Experience jumping
- Full suspension bikes with suspension in working order
- Full safety gear including pads (Full Face helmet not required, but suggested)

This class is intended for riders with jump experience and will move at a specified pace. Coaching staff reserves the right to hold riders to pre determined distances based on performance.

Please reach out if you are unsure if this class is a proper fit for you.

EventNotes:
Please read this!
 

Welcome to our FREE monthly ride! Ride start times vary by season to give us the best trail conditions and safest experience—May through September we roll out at 8:00 AM CT, and October through April we begin at 2:00 PM CT. We meet at the lower parking lot at Turkey Mountain Urban Wilderness Park, 6800 S Elwood Ave, Tulsa, OK 74132. Restrooms are available.

 

We will have ride leaders for skill levels between Beginner to Advanced. If you're new to mountain biking, OR have never taken WeROK’s Fundamentals, or other formal fundamentals skills clinics (even if you have been riding some), we REQUIRE YOU to start with the WeROK Fundamental Skills Session during registration. Regardless of your riding experience we feel taking this skills session will help improve your riding and create a better riding experience for all.

 

Loaner Bikes: Please refer to your registration confirmation letter. 
 

Cancellation/Bad Weather Policy: If bad weather develops we aim to cancel the event by 6:00 am the day of the ride.  Stay tuned to social media for announcements. We also follow Trailbot, in case Turkey Mountain trails are “closed” or “delayed”.  We do not have “rain dates”. 

 

Choosing appropriate group: First choose your riding and fitness level, then choose the best description among the groups. Once a group fills, the waitlist option will open. If you have a friend with the same skill level with whom you want to ride, help us out by registering together ASAP, in the same ride level, AND in same group number. Other than cancellations, we CANNOT GUARANTEE we can make any changes to groups, especially at the last minute, since we have group size restrictions. This delivers the best possible ride experience for all! If you don't end up riding with your friends, don't worry, you'll have the opportunity to make new ones!
 

Not sure which group to join? Ride levels are based on YOUR CURRENT skill and endurance levels. We want everyone to have the best and safest experience possible so we use a “rating” system to help align you with the right ride group. Please review the skills, endurance, mileage and proposed trails. Being in the right group makes a better, safer ride for all. If you are still unsure about which group might be for you just contact us at ride@werok.org. P.S. It is perfectly fine to “repeat” a level! Mastery of ALL levels takes time and practice. Please don’t rush yourself, nor succumb to peer pressure. NOTE: WeROK’s skill level names and colors are relative to Turkey Mountain trails. Other trail systems’ color designations could mean their Blue is (y)our Black, so be wise!
 

Advancing to next groups: A great way to know if you are ready to progress to the next ride level is if (1) you felt comfortable with skills necessary at your current level, and (2) you were able to keep up with the ride leader the entire ride and felt like you could have ridden longer. 

 

GROUP CHOICES:
 

1. FUNDAMENTAL SKILLS SESSION 

Select this group if you have never ridden a mountain bike, it’s been longer than you’d like to admit, OR you've never taken any type of basic mtb skills lessons before. Welcome! You have to start somewhere and this is the place! Even the most advanced riders should brush up on these essentials, and certainly, if you feel rusty, this session will help you. This session will cover the fundamentals of mountain biking, and then you'll hit the trail for a 2-3 mile ride. Successful completion of WeROK’s Fundamentals (or its equivalent) is required for advancement to next groups. Departure from this policy requires approval by a WeROK ride leader.

  • Skill Level: Beginner.
  • Pedals: Flat pedals are required (we may have loaner pedals available; email us ahead of time at ride@werok.org).
  • Skills you can perform: no requirement, you will definitely learn a skill or two after this session. 
  • Fitness Level: No requirement other than participate in possible heat for up to 2 hours.
  • Example of Turkey Mountain terrain: Packed dirt, no rocks; double track near Bomb Cellar; the grassy fields; the Family Loop; the lower “mini-switchback-berm” loop. 

2. FUNDAMENTALS TO GREEN Group

Select this group if you have taken the Fundamental Skills session, you feel more confident with those skills, and you are looking for a very easy-going transition to green trails. You will have a skills refresher for up to 15 minutes.

  • Skill Level: Confident Beginner.
  • Pedals: Flat pedals strongly encouraged (see above re: loaner pedals).
  • Skills you can perform: Staying upright while pedaling, skills learned in Fundamentals Group are beginning to make sense, and your confidence is growing.
  • Fitness Level: Completed a Fundamentals session with minimal fatigue
  • Examples of Turkey Mountain terrain: Packed dirt with occasional flat, mellow rocks or roots, no significant downhill or uphill; Family Loop; the lower “mini-switchback-berm” loop; the very first section of LoChi Connector.
  • Duration: 3-5 miles, maybe longer in cooler weather, no longer than 1.5 hours after refresher portion

3. GREEN Group
You’ve ridden on the dirt trails multiple times by now, and you’re getting the hang of things. You’re mastering the Fundamentals Skills, and your bike operating and handling skills feel smoother. No Fundamentals refresher portion provided.

  • Skill level: Beginner Plus.
  • Pedals: Flat pedals preferred.
  • Skills you can perform: Level pedals while coasting; one finger braking; becoming more comfortable with neutral and ready positions; and smoother corners/berms.
  • Fitness level: Able to ride steady at a comfortable pace for 30 minutes on easy terrain, and may need a breather while climbing, or at the top.
  • Examples of Turkey Mountain terrain: Packed dirt with a variety of low, smooth surface changes; more variety of up and downhill; LoChi; UHF or All Up with rests.
  • Duration: 5-7 miles,1.5 to 2.0 hours 

4. OPEN Group

Looking for new challenges! You are ready to explore more trail features (obstacles) and a variety of up and downhills, with limited stops. Mileage varies. No Fundamentals refresher provided. 

  • Skill level: Beginner Plus-to-Intermediate.
  • Pedals: Flat pedals preferred.
  • Skills you can perform: GREEN skills are solid, but you’re out of saddle more instinctively with level pedals; in and out of neutral/ready position more smoothly; frequent appropriate shifting; smoother, smoother berms and corners; want to ride across straight bridges and skinnies 3-5 feet wide; comfortable choosing lines through rockier terrain, or between tight trees.
  • Fitness level: You’re riding a few times a week. Can ride a WeROK course continuously unless learning steep or more technical terrain. Pushing the pace uphill.
  • Examples of Turkey Mountain terrain: Packed dirt, more roots and rocks, twists and turns. The small bridge on OLD Lo Chi, All Up, UHF, Stay Gold Loop, Naharkey clockwise, maybe counterclockwise. Sessioning features within your skill set, such as the small skinny on Family Loop.
  • Duration: 8-10 miles, 2 hours with some stopping.

EventName: Tacchino Ciclocross -- Event #7 of the 2026 BikeReg Cyclocross Super Series
EventNotes:
The Venue:  we have an exciting venue -- the Montgomery County Agricultural History Farm Park, which provides us with lots of terrain and options for fun and challenging cyclocross features.

Parking:  parking will be adjacent to the course. Look for signs at the entrance.

Alcohol Prohibited!  The venue is a Montgomery County park.  Park regulations prohibit alcohol. Please do not jeopardize our use of the park.

Food Trucks:   There will be at least one food truck and we are working on more. 

Medical/First Aid:  There will be EMT support on-site.  First aid will be available at the registration shelter. 

The Event:  Tacchino Ciclocross is a BikeReg Cyclocross Super Series event.  The event is held under USA Cycling permit #16399.  All USAC Cyclocross rules apply. Event will be held rain or shine.  Prizes will be awarded as soon as possible after each event.  Please remain near the podiums following your race if you place.  The start of the protest period will be announced. 

Course Description:  The course will be classic Mid-Atlantic.  There are rolling hills, a challenging section through the woods, numerous off-cambers, gravel paths, and at least one set of obstacles.  There will be one double-sided pit on the course.

****PROFESSIONAL CHIP TIMING by Insight Timing Services****

Registration, Entry Fees, & Licensing:  all registration and payment for this event, including race day registration, will be conducted through BikeReg.  Addtional entries are offered at $20 ($25 on race day) when purchased in the same BikeReg shopping cart.  If the entries are purchased separately during the pre-registration period, contact us for a partial refund; on event day a coupon code will be made available at the day-of registration table to achieve the same discounted price.  Entry fees will increase to $50 for adults and $25 for Juniors for race day registration, to reflect the day-of surcharge.  There will be no in-person sales at the event -- register online, either at home before coming out or on your phone at the event.  You MUST present your racing license (if you have one) or 1-Day receipt in order to be issued a bib, and you should also be prepared to show your confirmation email.  In order to expedite your entry, make sure you have completed the online waiver before approaching the day-of registration table. 

This page will re-open for late/day-of registration in the afternoon of the Friday prior to the event.  Race day registration and check-in will open by 7:30 AM.  Check-in and registration for all races will close 20 minutes prior to the scheduled start of the race.  There will be no exceptions made to this rule -- plan to show up timely for the race you want to enter.

A USA Cycling racing license is required for entry.  Riders who do not provide a USAC Annual racing license # at registration will be assessed an additional $15 for a Beginner 1-Day license.  This license is valid for entry only in fields that are open to Novice Men, Women, or Non-Binary riders.  For all other fields, you must present proof of an active USAC racing license showing your Cyclocross category and Racing Age.

Any current National Cyclocross Champions shall be granted free entry, but must wear their national jersey in the class in which it was won.

Series Points:  SuperSeries points are awarded for all races EXCEPT the Novice Men and Cat. 4/Novice Women races.

On-Course Warmup:  riders shall only enter the course for warmup laps between races in the designated area near the starting grid.  The gate will be the only entry point to the course and entry time will be designated by the race officials.

Staging:  riders shall be staged in order of their assigned bib number.  Tacchino CX is the 7th event of the 2026 BikeReg Cyclocross SuperSeries.  In fields eligible for SuperSeries points, bibs will be assigned to the first 8 riders (i.e., the front row) in order of their position in the Super Series standings on CrossResults.com ( https://www.crossresults.com/superseries ); remaining riders will be assigned bibs in order of the riders’ CrossResults.com ranking points; any remaining unranked riders will be assigned bibs by registration date & time.  For the Novice Men & Cat. 4/Novice Women, riders will be assigned bibs by registration date & time.  For all race categories, the first 4 positions in the third row are optionally available to the Race Director for discretionary call-ups.  Race day entries will be assigned remaining bib numbers on a first come, first served basis; riders registering on race day are not entitled to special treatment based on their position in the SuperSeries points standings or their CrossResults.com ranking.

Staging Procedure:  riders will fill the starting grid by bib number, 8 riders at a time, as specified in the USA Cycling Cyclocross rulebook when so directed by the officials; the officials will fill any gaps left by DNS or late-arriving riders as appropriate.  ALL RIDERS MUST ASSEMBLE IN THE PRE-STAGING CHUTE NO LATER THAN 10 MINUTES BEFORE THEIR START!   Riders arriving late to staging may be staged at the back of the starting grid at discretion of the Chief Referee.

MABRA Mission Statement:

“To promote the sport of bicycle racing in the Mid-Atlantic region, principally within the states of Delaware and Maryland, the northern portion of the state of Virginia, the eastern panhandle of West Virginia, and the District of Columbia;

To foster camaraderie and fellowship among culturally, racially and gender diverse bicycle racers and enthusiasts within the Mid-Atlantic;

To help ensure bicycle racers and enthusiasts in the Mid-Atlantic have an equal opportunity to participate in bicycle racing and activity without discrimination on the basis of race, color, religion, age, gender, sexual orientation, or national origin;

To support and facilitate the efforts of its members, clubs, and other organizations that promote diverse, inclusive and equitable bicycle racing/activity/engagement in the Mid-Atlantic;

To support the efforts of its members in promoting bicycle racing and events for local, regional, national and international competition; and

To undertake such actions as are necessary, proper, desirable, advisable, or convenient for the furtherance and accomplishment of the foregoing purposes, provided that such actions do not exceed the bounds accepted for a District of Columbia nonprofit corporation.” 

* The 150 rider limit is for the combined field in a race.  Registration will close once the limit has been reached by any combination of classes within the field. 

* Classes designated “Masters” are open to Men and Women. Minimum Racing Age and categories quoted are for Men; minimum Racing Age and categories for Women per USAC rules.

** Promoter reserves the right to increase total prize purse as race day gets closer.

Gender Equality & Transgender Policy: 

Classes designated “Masters” are open to Men and Women. The minimum Racing Age and categories quoted are for Men; please see the current USAC Rulebook for minimum Racing Age and categories for Women.  The Super Series  welcomes everyone to participate in the gender category they feel is most appropriate to them, as described in USA Cycling policies: https://usacycling.org/about-us/governance/transgender-athletes-policy

The collective teams comprising the MABRA Super Series are committed to providing inclusive and equitable racing events.  The Super Series is proudly adding non-binary categories (1/2/3 and 4/5) to race during the women's races.  This addition is to honor all of our cyclists and provide a category that allows everyone to race with how they identify.  

In the event that USAC chooses to amend current policy to align with UCI changes for our transgender racers, then WTF (women-trans-femme) will be added to our non-binary categories as WTFNB.

Thanks for signing up to volunteer at this month WeROK MTB Group ride!  Our start times change with the seasons—because the mountain rides best when it wants to. May through September we roll out at 9:00 AM CT, and October through April we begin at 2:00 PM CT.  We look forward to riding with you soon! 

 

Meeting Location: Lower Lot, Turkey Mountain Urban Wilderness Park 6800 S Elwood Ave, Tulsa, OK 74132
 

Please come to the ride with your name written in big letters on masking tape.
 

Please arrive 30 minutes prior to ride start time so we can be ready when the participants arrive.
 

Upon arrival, please pick up a Yellow Vest and rest your bike by your group sign.  The riders will be looking for their groups by approaching the ride leaders/sweepers with Yellow Vest. Groups will be spread out, all leaving from the same field but in the small group you lead.

 

Things to remember:

  • Check your bike and bring a working mountain bike.
  • Bring a water bottle or water bladder pack.
  • Feel free to bring snacks and beverages of your choice for Post Ride Social gathering.


Thank you for volunteering!  Let's Ride Bikes!

#WeROK #beYoudoYouforYou #YouBelong

Why Join?

  • Team clothing with on-line ordering windows.
  • Discounted entry fees for the Charlie Baker Time Trial
  • Access to e-mail lists for answers to even the most obscure questions about training, nutrition, technique, equipment, and the rules of racing.
  • USAC Officials support in the form of license reimbursement for new and current officials
  • Please visit https://www.facebook.com/northeastbicycle/ for updates

For more info on the Club, browse through our web site and be sure to visit the About NEBC page, and the list of NEBC news archives. Or send us a note at NortheastBicycleClub@gmail.com.

You can also join us for the monthly club BOD meetings.

EventNotes:
Fall is the best time to ride bikes

  • CCAP School Clubs begin riding in September
  • Teams ride together in a supportive positive environment led by USA Cycling certified coaches
  • Riders learn to improve their skills and stamina along with bicycle and trail maintenance
  • Clubs practice twice a week
  • Two group ride adventure trips are scheduled:
    • Bluff Point in Groton, CT
    • Watrous Park in Cromwell, CT

A properly fitting bicycle helmet and mountain bike in good working condition are required.  This gear can be provided if your junior rider does not have currently have a helmet or bicycle.

All families joining a CCAP Program are required to adhere to CCAP Protocols.  These are found in the waivers section of the online registration form on BikeReg.  Please review and confirm with your signature.

WCC Membership 2026 

WestCoast Cycling Society (WCC) has been primarily a mountain bike club for many years, but with the reduction in XC racing and activity, we have transitioned into a road, gravel and Cyclocross focused group.  We still do mountain biking, but opportunities for racing are somewhat limited.
A previous requirement for membership with WCC was a Competition License or General Membership with Cycling BC (CBC).  Since 2025, this requirement has been dropped.  We no longer require a CBC membership or license to join WCC. There is no distinction between licensed and non-licensed members.
WCC is officially affiliated with CBC, the benefit of this is that we can put on races under the stewardship of CBC.  This requires that at least one member of WCC must hold a Competition and Technical License with CBC, a condition that we do indeed meet.

There is always support for anyone that wants to organize an event, a ride or an adventure that club members can participate in.  Some that come to mind …. weeknight Mt.  Seymour Road climbs, a mid summer Mt. Baker climb (followed by burgers or ice-cream), North Shore Mountain bike epics and local gravel escapades.

More General benefits for WCC membership. 
-  Opportunity to join and connect with members for recreational and racing opportunities
-  No charge (as in free) entry into any racing events organized and run by WCC.  Club members all chip in to help organize and run events as well as race (the primary objective).  Vanier Park CX is our primary event focus.
-  We have a great relationship with Schwalbe Tyres which results in us being able to order great tires to keep us all running rubber side down, all with a decent discount.   https://www.schwalbetires.com/
-  Blonyx Canada has been good enough to support our members with a 25% Discount on their nutrition and supplement products.  The discount code is sent out monthly and can be paired with they existing 15% subscription discount.  I can vouch for the electrolyte and the protein powder (NO Stevia …. yipee).    https://blonyx.ca/
-  While limited in scope, we also have a sponsorship arrangement with RaceFace Easton for discounts on parts and accessories.  Again, it helps with keeping our bikes running and up to date.      https://www.raceface.ca/

Welcome to Larz Cyclocross Practice! We meet at the top of the hill at Larz Anderson Park in Brookline, by the parking lot. It will be the same format, with a 6:45AM preride, with 2x20' heats starting at 7AM, ending by 8AM sharp. Open to all ability levels.

Rules: 

  1. We may cancel Larz at any point in time, for any reason. Weather is usually the reason though; these cancellations will be made by 7PM on Tuesday, if not earlier.
  2. Park is open to dog walkers, runners, and other users - give them the right of way and be nice at all times!
  3. Bring a good attitude and a desire to go HAAHD.

West Texas Showdown

Terlingua, TX | Dec. 4th - 6th, 2026

The West Texas Showdown isn’t just a race — it’s a battle against the desert itself. Big Bend delivers jagged singletrack, endless horizons, and conditions as raw as they come. Wild, unpredictable, and unforgiving — this is where legends are made.

The third stage of the Texas Showdown Series and the crown jewel of the Texas Showdown Triple Crown.  Set in the Big Bend region of Texas, this event promises to test every ounce of grit, skill, and determination.

This is mountain desert country — wild, remote, and raw. The terrain is rugged, the weather unpredictable, and resources are scarce. Nearly everything in the desert either bites, pinches, stings, or grabs. Don’t be scared — but don’t come unprepared.

Big Bend – Home of the Showdown

Big Bend Ranch State Park and the surrounding desert country embody the spirit of West Texas: wide-open basins framed by volcanic cliffs, deep canyons carved by the Rio Grande, and horizons that shift with every mile.

It’s one of the most remote places in the lower 48, where solitude comes naturally and silence is as striking as the scenery. Out here, self-reliance isn’t optional — it’s survival. By day, the desert unfolds in stark beauty: ocotillo stretching skyward, hidden springs tucked into arroyos, and dirt roads that climb to vistas you’ll never forget. By night, you’ll ride under one of the darkest skies in North America, the Milky Way blazing overhead in a show few places on Earth can match.

Event Options

Showdown – 390 miles of Glory & Pain
This is the flagship route: long, raw, and unrelenting. It starts with a paved rollout from Terlingua before plunging straight into the wilds of Big Bend Ranch State Park. Riders will grind up gravel park roads, hike through rugged arroyos, and battle through stretches of singletrack where “rideable” depends on your skill, stamina, and stubbornness.

Highlights:

  • Marfa (Mile ~200): A quirky West Texas art town, home of the mysterious “Marfa Lights” and the famous Prada “storefront.” Will quite literally be a desert oasis for riders.
  • Pinto Canyon: One of the most dramatic landscapes in Texas. A twisting, jaw-dropping descent through volcanic cliffs. Sunrise or sunset here is unforgettable.
  • Rio Grande Stretch: Long paved miles along the border, with Mexico just across the river. Stunning views and a glimpse of life in the small border towns.
  • The Death Loop: A 50-mile finale north of Terlingua that will test what’s left of your legs and your willpower.

Stats: ~390 miles | 60% unpaved / 40% paved

Slowdown – 290 miles of Dust & Determination
A shorter, but still fierce route through Big Bend. The Slowdown trims the distance but keeps the character: gravel park roads, rough country tracks, stretches of arroyo riding, and just enough singletrack to keep you honest. This is a full-on bike expedition into one of the harshest and most beautiful places in the country.

Highlights:

  • Remote gravel stretches deep inside Big Bend Ranch SP
  • Rough, sandy arroyos that force you to wrestle with your bike as much as ride it
  • Expansive desert views that make every climb worth it
  • Just enough pavement to catch your breath before the dirt pulls you back in

Stats: ~290 miles | 48% unpaved / 52% paved

Lowdown – The Gateway to Big Bend
 The Lowdown is our non-competitive, guided bikepacking group ride. Designed to introduce riders to the magic of Big Bend in a slightly more approachable way. This route is not to be taken lightly, the distance is shorter, but the miles are hard. A good option for those with experience bikepacking, but want to try something more extreme.

Ride leaders and sweepers will help guide the way, but this is still a self-supported trip. You’ll need to carry your own food, water, and camping gear. Along the way you’ll experience the vastness, solitude, and starlit skies that make Big Bend unforgettable.

Highlights:

  • Long stretches of gravel roads and dry arroyos inside Big Bend Ranch SP
  • Nights spent under some of the darkest skies in North America
  • Bring your big tires and probably suspension

Stats: ~85 miles over 3 days | 80% unpaved / 20% paved

Schedule

Thursday, Dec. 3rd

  • 12–8pm: Rider check-in & tracker pickup
     
  • 8–9pm: Pre-race meeting at TBD

Friday, Dec. 4th

  • 7am: Showdown & Slowdown & Lowdown - Grand Departs

Saturday, Dec. 5th

  • All day: Ride Your Damn Bike

Sunday, Dec. 6th

  • All day: Celebrate finishers at Temple of the Bird
     
  • 5pm: Hoedown starts w/ live local music
     
  • 7–8pm: Awards + raffle
     
  • 10pm: Party winds down
     

Host City & HQ

Our host town is Terlingua, TX — a once-thriving mercury mining hub turned ghost town, now home to a small but eclectic community of artists, adventurers, and desert dreamers. Nestled between Big Bend Ranch State Park and Big Bend National Park, Terlingua’s ruins, shacks, and quirky dwellings create a setting unlike anywhere else.

Race HQ will be at the Temple of the Bird and it'll be our home for the weekend.

Getting Here

Terlingua is off the beaten path — there are no direct planes, trains, or buses. The nearest airports are in Midland or El Paso; from there, it’s a long desert drive. If you’re arriving via Alpine or Marfa, you’ll also pass through a Border Patrol checkpoint before reaching town.

Rider Notes

  • Bike Choice: This is MTB country — rocky climbs, rugged singletrack, arroyo crossings, and rough gravel. Leave your gravel bike at home.
  • Self-Supported: Riders must carry food, water, navigation, and repair gear. Resources are extremely limited.
  • Leave No Trace: The desert is fragile. Pack it in, pack it out. No catholing. Carry a waste bag.
  • Risks: Remote terrain, wildlife, weather extremes, and isolation. This is not an event for the faint of heart or the unprepared.
     

FAQ

Why don’t the routes go into Big Bend National Park?
Bikes are not allowed on singletrack trails inside the National Park. All riding is on roads only. Big Bend Ranch State Park offers far better opportunities for rugged, off-road adventure.  The National Park is also not open to these types of events…yet!

Will I pass through a Border Patrol checkpoint?
Yes. If you’re driving in from Alpine or Marfa, you will pass through a permanent Border Patrol checkpoint north of Terlingua. Have your ID handy.  You will also have a Border checkpoint if you are doing the Showdown or Slowdown heading into Marfa.  

What’s the weather like in December?
Riders should be prepared for temperatures ranging from below freezing overnight to warm, sun-filled afternoons. Weather in Big Bend Ranch State Park can change rapidly, and strong winds, cold rain, and freezing temperatures are all possible. Conditions may vary dramatically across the route due to changes in elevation, terrain, and exposure.

? What bike should I bring?
This is MTB terrain. Wide tires, suspension, and durable gear are highly recommended. Gravel bikes will not cut it here.

? How self-supported is this event?
Completely. Riders are expected to carry their own food, water, tools, and navigation. Resupply points are limited, so plan carefully. Rescue vehicles will be available to extract riders off course if needed, but when you're riding, you're on your own!

? How do I handle waste?
Big Bend’s desert ecosystem is delicate. Riders must follow Leave No Trace principles. That means packing out all trash and carrying a waste bag — no catholing allowed.

EventNotes:
The legendary New England Cyclocross Finale Returns for its 19th year!
 

 

49% of extremely biased twitteratti agree:  this race is basically the World Championships


Hey, you probably noticed from the category names that this isn't a USAC sanctioned event.   If you can't figure out what field to register for, the answer is either "Beginner" or "Singlespeed."  Or you can always email us any questions using the "contact event" link above.  

 

What's with the name?:

It's a combination of this and that.


Who races when??  How do I win money? 

  • Jedi Men and Jedi 40+ Men will race together (1 start) with 40+ denoted in results.  Shared prize list of $500 with $100 bonus cash for 40+.

  • Jedi Women and Jedi 40+ Women will race together (1 start) with 40+ denoted in results.  Shared prize list of $500 with $100 bonus cash for 40+

  • Singlespeed men, fat bikes and women will race together (2 starts) with separate results and prizes.

  • Riders can race in additional races for $20.

  • Start positions determined by rider rankings at crossresults.com

  • Mountain Bikes allowed in any category.  Even if they have bar ends.  Unless the bar ends have pointy knives on them.

What's new this year?

We have a food truck (Thai Chili)!  

There's a bunch of new weird motocross lines and piles of dirt to play with!  We don't know exactly how we're going to use it all yet, but we do know it's gonna be good.

What's your inclusivity policy?

Ice Weasels is a celebration of cyclocross that everyone should feel welcome to be a part of.  Athletes are encouraged to show up and and race as their authentic selves in whatever category makes the most sense to them.

We have a zero tolerance policy for harassment so if anyone is being a jerk about anyone's identity (or anything else for that matter) let us know and we'll take care of it.
 


What's your refund policy?

We grant all refunds, all the time, for any reason.  Missing the race is punishment enough, we don't need to rub it in by keeping your money.  If you're on the fence, just register now (before your field is full!) and ask for a refund if you change your mind.

 

Remember how awesome last year was?

Welcome to the Pie Ride!

Keo, Arkansas • Saturday, December 5, 2026

Nestled in Southern Lonoke County (SoLoCo), Keo is a bike-friendly town of just 207 residents that knows how to roll out the welcome mat. We’re glad you’re here to ride, celebrate, and of course—eat pie!

Routes

  • SoLoCo 25

https://ridewithgps.com/routes/52192236

  • SoLoCo 35

https://ridewithgps.com/routes/52192137

Start Line

The ride begins at 10:00 AM sharp from the Keo Airstrip on Pecan Road. The airstrip is located just half a mile east of town at the intersection of Pecan Road and Cemetery Road.

Pre-Ride Happy Hour

  • When: Wednesday, December 2
  • Where: Moody Brews 414 E. 21st Street, Pettaway Square, Little Rock, AR.
  • Time: 4:00 PM – 7:00 PM

We are celebrating Happy Hour at Moody Brews and want to introduce you to a really cool partnership between the brewery, South Lonoke County (SoLoCo) and the Pie Ride! Moody Brews gets their rice for their New Ground Pils from Isbell Farms, located in SoLoCo. Brewer Josiah Moody then transforms that rice into New Ground Pils, a light lager, which will be served at the Pecan Festival. We are going green this year and only providing a bib number, safety pins and a drop bag to be used on ride day. Drop your street clothes at the start line and they will be at the Finish Line to change into for the Festival. 

Did You Come to Get Your Nuts Cracked?

Grab the official 2026 Arkansas Pecan Festival tee! Printed on soft, 100% cotton, lived-in Comfort Colors shirt in green. This year's festival tee is one you'll actually want to wear long after festival day.  

$30 each - Sizes S-XL

Pre-order yours and pick it up at the Pre-Ride Happy Hour at Moody Brews, Wednesday, December 2nd or on festival day, December 5th, in Keo. Last day to order a shirt is November 30th.

Ride Morning

  • Check-In: Look for the Keo Collective at the Airstrip. They’ll get you to the start line on the runway. *Note, there will be a single toilet available at the Airstrip, please plan accordingly, extra facilities available a half mile west at the Festival.
  • Drop Bags: Write your name clearly on your bag and place any post-ride clothes or gear inside. Volunteers will transport it to the official Finish Line in downtown Keo at the Arkansas Pecan Festival. 

Finish Line Celebration

The ride officially ends in Keo, right in the heart of the Arkansas Pecan Festival. Secure your bike in the secure bike area, grab a Moody Brews pour, and savor your well-earned slice of pecan pie. Stick around to enjoy the festival’s car show, vendors, entertainment, and holiday cheer.

Important Note: You must register before November 23 to guarantee your slice of pie is reserved for you at the Finish Line.

After the Festival

When you’ve had your fill of pie and fun, noodle back at your own pace to the Keo Airstrip to retrieve your vehicle. Don’t forget to collect your drop bag with your kit, helmet, and shoes before heading out.

Registration opens Friday, June 12th at 8am with participation based on a first-come, first-served basis. To create a rewarding enduro race experience, organizers reserve the right to limit overall event participation.

  • Awards ceremony by category with prizes awarded 3 deep.

SAFETY - This is not the time to skimp on protective equipment. Helmets are required to be worn on course during official event times and we highly suggest a full-face helmet, knee pads, and elbow pads.

TEMPERATURE - In Bella Vista, Arkansas, December is relatively mild but chilly, with average daily highs in the upper 40s to low 50s (9°C to 10°C) and average overnight lows dropping into the 30s (0°C to 1°C)

Rapture in Misery: From 24 Hours of Madness to a Mountain Biking Legend

Celebrating the legacy of a race that became a rite of passage

It Started with a Wild Idea

In 2001, a loose-knit group of mountain bikers rolled into Snow Creek chasing something few could understand — and even fewer could finish. A 24-hour mountain bike race. No glory, no fame — just headlights, hills, and a lot of pain. The idea was simple: ride until you can't, then ride a little more.

That first Rapture in Misery lit a fire. And soon, it became more than just a race. It became a legend.

The First Ride – Snow Creek, 2001

There was something gritty and pure about that first year. Snow Creek, typically known for its winter ski runs, played host to a summer sufferfest. Riders took turns circling a course that felt more like an endurance gauntlet than a bike race. People rode through the night, relying on duct tape, drive, and caffeine to hold themselves together.

There were no luxuries — just tents, cold sandwiches, and the sound of freehubs clicking through the darkness. If you were there, you still tell stories about it. If you weren’t, you’ve heard them.

Landahl Park – Technical, Raw, and Wild

After two years at Snow Creek, Rapture in Misery moved to Landahl Park, one of Missouri’s most revered singletrack trail systems. And with that shift, the race found a new kind of identity: raw, technical, and beautifully brutal.

Landahl’s terrain was a whole different animal. Tight turns, sharp climbs, off-camber descents — it wasn’t just about endurance anymore. It was about skill, timing, and knowing exactly how hard you could push without breaking... your bike or yourself.

Some came because they loved Landahl’s unforgiving charm. Others came because they’d heard about this crazy race where legends were made — and sometimes broken. Either way, it was a proving ground, and it helped cement Rapture as a must-do for Midwest endurance junkies.

Crowder State Park – Community Roots Deepen

Eventually, Rapture moved again in 2009 — this time to Crowder State Park, and with that move came a new phase. If Snow Creek was the spark and Landahl the fire, Crowder was where the fire turned into a tradition.

At Crowder, the vibe shifted from wild experiment to beloved annual gathering. The course was tough — don’t let anyone tell you otherwise — but there was something about it that brought people together. The campground felt like a mini-village each year, full of familiar faces, shared meals, and the occasional beer hand-up.

It was here that Rapture’s community really bloomed. Solo riders, team riders, rookies, and veterans all came together with a shared understanding: this race was something special.

More Than a Race – What Made RIM Special

What set Rapture in Misery apart wasn’t just the course, the miles, or the midnight hallucinations — it was the people.

There was something magnetic about the event that brought out the best (and sometimes the weirdest) in everyone. You’d see solo riders grinding out lap after lap with thousand-yard stares, and then laugh at a guy in a tutu sprinting for a handoff. You’d share tools, tubes, and war stories with people you’d just met.

It was more than a race. It was a reunion for the unreasonably driven — the community of “why-not?” people. Everyone suffered, and everyone smiled through it.

The Newest Chapter

Rapture and Misery will stay true to its roots. This years event will take place around lake Jacomo and Blue Springs lake. We will connect single track, road, and chat trail to complete a 50 to 60ish mile loop. The trails will encompass some of the areas hardest climbing and tech. Each rider will receive a t-shirt and food. The riders that finish before sunset will receive a finishers prize.

NO ONSITE REGISTRATION - BIKEREG ONLY

Racing is available for all ages and abilities.

Each racer, typically, will have the opportunity to race three (3) times during the event.

Typically, riders will race one Elimination race, one Scratch race, and one of the following types:  Scratch, Elimination, Keirin, Points, or Madison.

The specific race program will be determined when registration closes, based on the number and skill levels of participants.  This is done to ensure the best possible experience for racers.

Race fields are not restricted by gender or age, with the exception of "Young Juniors" races which are typically restricted to juniors under 14 years of age.

EventName: The Sandy Neck Fat Bike Winter Classic!
EventNotes:
Please Sign the online waiver!

PLEASE READ!!! 

EVERY QUESTION IS ANSWERED HERE!

After you are registered be sure to join this Strava Club: https://www.strava.com/clubs/466019/members.

 The Sandy Neck Fat Bike Winter Classic (SNFBWC) is back for a fun time!

 Way back when we first had this idea; to race Fat Bikes on Sandy Neck Beach in December we didn’t know it would double in size and still sell out so fast.

It's been sold out since 2019, so you know we are going to do something new to commemorate it. Funny apparel is encouraged.

The 2026 edition of our 15.74-mile party ride will follow nearly the same route as last year - zigzagging back and forth across Sandy Neck, out to the Lighthouse and back to the parking lot. 

 - START TIME IS NOON.  

 Online registration only. Check in begins at 10:30am on race day.

 Ride begins at noon with a mass start roll out on the beach. We expect all participants to finish and safely exit the Sandy Neck course by 3:30pm, long before the sun sets. If you think it will take you longer than 3-½ hours to complete, please tell an official at registration.

 All riders will be checked in at the beginning and, more importantly, MUST BE CHECKED OUT at the end of the course, because everybody has to be accounted for before the volunteers and Sandy Neck Ranger Staff can finish their day and join the after party and we don’t want to lose anybody!

 The lighthouse aid station will include a water bubbler for refilling your water bottles, cookies or brownies, and maybe more. Note that the lighthouse is on private property, so we can have all kinds of fun. The aid station will close at 2:30pm. Again: Everybody has to be off the race course by 3:30pm and checked off by a race official as having safely completed the ride. 

 If you want to compete for a prize:  the race component of this party ride is a sprint starting 100 yards or so from the race start and ending on the beach just before you get to the lighthouse. This is also the first of two Strava segments (https://www.strava.com/segments/42494298 ).

 Since that’s it for racing, you’re welcome to hang out at the Lighthouse longer and have more fun!

 The second segment will stay up for bragging rights but will not be part of the race. It starts after exiting the lighthouse driveway and ends 100 yards or so before the Sandy Neck Gatehouse, which is the end of the race and where you will be checked off by an official (https://www.strava.com/segments/42493363).

 Winners of the sprint will be determined by a race official at the finish line. Small prizes will go to the top three women and top three men.

 Intersections will be clearly marked with arrows and/or race tape. While the elevation on this route is minimal, the challenge is grinding through several long stretches of deep, sugary sand. There are few short walk up ascents and a bunch of exciting but short descents.

 All proceeds for SNFBWC will benefit the Cape Cod chapter of NEMBA (https://nemba-capecod.org/).

 All participants are required to wear a helmet and carry phones with ringers on in case of emergency and to help us account for you if you aren’t checked off at race end for whatever reason. 

 

Directions to the start: 
From 6A in East Sandwich, follow Sandy Neck Road past the Gatehouse to the main parking lot at the end of the road. 

The address is:  Sandy Neck Beach, West Barnstable, MA 02668.

 

Post-ride party will be at a location (Off the Grid) and have a cash bar but dinner is included, 2 signature SNFBWC  beverages from Independent Fermentations Brewing will be picked up at registration.  All riders and volunteers get a newly designed 2026 commemorative item.

 

Party location: Off the Grid

91 MA-6A, Sandwich, MA 02563

 

 

 

Rain or Shine - No Refunds

 

Additional useful information:

At a casual pace, the route will take most people well under three hours. The race route is about 7 miles, short race=more hanging out time at the lighthouse.

Check the weather and dress appropriately.

The difficulty of the route is largely dependent on the temperature and the moisture content of the sand. 

There are a half dozen or so challenging but short hike-a-bikes.

Bailouts are permitted as long as you check out at the end, but the route is only 15 miles and we encourage you to ride the whole thing.

A Sandy Neck ranger and a bicycle mechanic will follow the race in case there are any situations requiring assistance.

No tire size regulations - ride whatever you want. However, the Town of Barnstable prohibits Ebikes on Sandy Neck. 

We recommend lowering your tire pressure, depending on your weight, to 4 to 6 PSI, or, as low as you can go without hitting your rims.

Pre-Ride:  https://www.strava.com/segments/42497402. NOTE:  The section from Trail 6 around the point of Sandy Neck to the Lighthouse has been changed. When you see a ‘No Bikes’ sign, respect it and continue on the main trail to the green street sign “Judson Norse Rd” take a sharp left. This is a very special day, the one time a year we get to ride around the point to the Sandy Neck Lighthouse!

EventNotes:
Register now to be part of the best XC Endurance event in Oklahoma - Dam Zombies.  Choose your adventure: 3 Hour Solo, 6 Hour Solo or 6 Hour Team. This year we are adding special NICA categories to allow for our youth to compete against each other on their own separate course. What's more is a NICA Family Team category - where a NICA Athlete and adult (coach, mentor, parent) can team up and compete with other NICA Family teams.   NICA and Non-NICA will only share the pit zone and start finish trails - no overlapping the single track for Veteran Zombies and Fresh Zombies (NICA). By popular demand, I've added an e-bike category; e-bikes will race the non-NICA course with the other “veteran zombies." 

What to expect: Line up at 10:00 for the 6-hour mass start, or 1:00 for the 3-hour solo mass start. Ride as many complete laps as you can within the 3 or 6 hours. The winner is the most laps within the time limits. Tied for laps? The winner is the who completed their full laps first (fastest clock time).  Take as many breaks as you like to rest or fuel up, get maintenance done, or switch out a bike (don't forget to move your number plate). Teams - Only one team member riding the course at a time. Team members can rotate as often as you like (each lap, every few laps or half the race - you decide). Only catch is each team member must ride a minimum of one lap. 

The Pit Zone - set up your team tent, grab some hot pancakes for a donation from the NICA grill. Stick around for the end of the race for complimentary BBQ. All registrants will receive a custom I Survived Dam Zombies long sleeve tee. Custom trophies for 1st, 2nd, and 3rd place for all categories.  Out on the course Gearhead Outfitters will be providing neutral support Skratch Hydration - grab a cup on the go or stop and fill up your bottle. 

The Dam Zombies never disappoints - be sure to be one of the first 100 to register to claim one of the awesome custom shirts. 

 

- Turbo Joe (event director)

EventName: Capital `Cross Classic -- Event #8 of the 2026 BikeReg Cyclocross Super Series and MABRA Cat Champs
EventNotes:
The Bike Lane Presents

2026 Capital `Cross Classic Cyclocross Race

To Benefit Trails in Lake Fairfax Park

Finals of the 2026 BikeReg Super Series and MABRA Category Champs

Sunday, December 6, 2026, Lake Fairfax Park, Reston, VA

 

General Info

The 2026 Capital ‘Cross Classic is a USAC cyclocross event. All USAC rules and penalties apply. As the rider, you are responsible for knowing the rules for the race in which you are racing.

Beneficiary: Proceeds will benefit the Lake Fairfax Sustainable Natural Trail System program, which aims to build new sustainable trails and restore existing trails in Lake Fairfax Park.


Venue and amenities: The Capital Cross Classic course is located on the grounds of Lake Fairfax Park in Reston, Va. Heated restrooms, food vendor, a beer garden and free drinking water will be available onsite throughout the day. Alcohol is prohibited in the park, except in designated areas. There is a children’s playground located near the racecourse. As the event is a benefit for the park’s trails, attendees are encouraged to explore the miles of trails available in the park during their visit.

Parking: Parking is available in lots located off Lake Fairfax Drive in the park. Parking is free, IF course conditions are dry. However, the promoter reserves the right to institute a mandatory $2/vehicle parking fee if the course is soft or muddy and could suffer significant damage during the event. Capital ‘Cross Classic is a benefit for trail building and maintenance and it is the goal of the promoters to leave no trace of our use of the park. All damage to the park [turf, etc] will be paid for with proceeds from the race. If a parking fee is instituted, those funds will only be used to repair the course and/or benefit trails. Announcements regarding a parking fee will be made on the BikeReg.com registration page prior to the race. All racers and other attendees are encouraged to bring $2/vehicle to the race, just in case.

Team Parking: Team parking is available in close proximity to the racecourse. Please contact the promoter no later than one week in advance for team parking reservations. Team parking spots will be offered on a first-come-first-served basis.

Warm-ups: For the safety and courtesy of all racers, warming up on the course during races is prohibited. Violators will be disqualified. The course will be open for warm-ups during the 15 minutes preceding each race, if no racers remain on course.

Staging Procedure: Riders will fill the starting grid by bib number, 8 riders at a time, as specified in the USA Cycling Cyclocross rulebook when so directed by the officials; the officials will fill any gaps left by DNS or late-arriving riders as appropriate. All riders must assemble in the pre-staging chute no later than 10 minutes before their start. Riders arriving late to staging will be staged at the back of the starting grid.

Call-ups: You MUST pre-register if you want a call-up. For categories that award series points, the first 8 bibs (i.e., the front row) will be assigned to the top 8 pre-registered riders on series points.  Remaining pre-registered riders will be staged by CrossResults ranking.  Late/day-of riders will be staged by bib number, in the order of registration. The Men Cat. 5 and Women Cat. 4/5 categories will be staged by entry date & time for pre-registered riders, followed by late/day-of riders in the order of registration.  All categories will reserve four spots in the third row, which are to be used for promoters' discretionary call-ups.

Barrier Primes: Prizes will be awarded to the first rider in each field to clear the barriers cleanly on the first lap. For combined fields or fields that start simultaneously, one winner will be determined for that group. Winners MUST report immediately to the finish/podium area to claim their prizes. This will take place immediately after you finish. Failure to do so will result in a forfeit of your prize. Primes will be judged by race staff, not USA Cycling officials.

Series Points: Points are awarded for BikeReg Super Series rankings for all categories except Men Cat. 4 and Women Cat. 4/5.

Podium Finishers: The top finishers in every event MUST report immediately to the finish/podium area for awards and interviews. This will take place immediately after you finish and only last a few minutes. Failure to do so will result in a forfeit of your prizes.

BikeReg Super Series Top Finishers: Capital ‘Cross Classic is the series final for the BikeReg Super Series.

This event is held under USA Cycling permit 16497, pending.  

Course Info

The course is roughly 3km in length and consists of a paved start, grass and hard pack terrain, gravel paths, climbs, descents and some off-camber turns. The course will feature both man-made and natural obstacles.

Registration, Scoring, and Schedule

License: a USA Cycling racing license is required for entry in all fields except Li'l Belgians.  Unlicensed riders will be assessed an additional $15 in their shopping cart for a Beginner 1-Day license during registration.  Unlicensed riders may only register for fields that are specifically identified as "1-Day license valid for entry."  Racing Age for Cyclocross is defined as the rider's age on December 31, 2027.

Entry Fees:  The pre-registration entry fee is $40 for adult races and $20 for Junior races.  Online registration by BikeReg.com.  Online registration closes Fri., December 4, 2026 at 8:30 AM.  BikeReg assesses a service charge for online registration. There are no refunds and no mail-in registration.    

This page will re-open for late registration in the afternoon of the Friday prior to the event.  Late entry fees will increase to $50 for adults and $25 for Juniors.  All sales will be conducted through BikeReg – there will be no in-person sales at the event.  Register at home on Saturday or Sunday before coming out, or on your phone at the event.
